caveats: DONKI flares are observed by GOES from Earth orbit. Flare class (C/M/X) is peak X-ray brightness at Earth, not radiation dose at Mars. The game uses SEP (proton) records for dose and flare class only as context.
DONKI notifications only report flares of about M5.0 and above, so smaller flares are not included.
Earth's warnings use the flares/CMEs that DONKI itself links to each SEP record. If the blast and the particles are on the same day, the game says the warning came too late.
The light delay is computed for the middle of each storm week from approximate orbit formulas.

science_missions.title: Fly the helicopter
science_missions.fact: NASA's Ingenuity helicopter made 72 flights on Mars (2021 to 2024). It was the first powered flight on another planet.
science_missions.source: NASA JPL, Ingenuity flight log (first flight 19 April 2021, flight 72 on 18 January 2024)

science_missions.title: Make oxygen from Martian air
science_missions.fact: Perseverance's MOXIE machine made 122 grams of oxygen from Mars air. That is about what a small dog breathes in 10 hours.
science_missions.source: NASA, 'NASA's Oxygen-Generating Experiment MOXIE Completes Mars Mission', 6 Sept 2023

science_missions.title: Photograph Martian clouds
science_missions.fact: On 2 February 2023, the Curiosity rover took the first clear photo of sun rays shining through clouds on Mars.
science_missions.source: NASA JPL, 'NASA's Curiosity Captures First Sun Rays on Mars', March 2023

science_missions.title: Collect a rock sample
science_missions.fact: A sample is a small piece of rock kept for study. Perseverance seals rock cores in tubes so a future mission could bring them to Earth.
science_missions.source: NASA Mars 2020 Perseverance mission, sample collection

science_missions.title: Measure the radiation
science_missions.fact: Curiosity's RAD tool has measured radiation on Mars since 2012. Our 0.64 mSv per day comes from RAD.

science_missions.title: Check the Mars weather
science_missions.fact: Curiosity's weather station (REMS) measures air temperature, air pressure and wind in Gale crater.
science_missions.source: NASA Mars Science Laboratory, REMS instrument
